title: Goals in the City's published plans, and what has been reported against them
question: What did the homelessness and overdose plans promise by a stated date, and what do the City's own progress reports say?
finding: The homelessness department's 2017 and 2023 plans and Public Health's 2022 overdose plan state 38 dated goals and targets; a reported result could be found for 12 of them. Two years into the five-year homelessness plan, the department reports 10,300 people moved into permanent housing against a goal of 30,000 (five-year goal), and 15,186 given prevention help against 18,000 (five-year goal).
how: Goals, target dates and reported figures were transcribed from the plans and their progress reports by the download step, each with its page: the homelessness department's Strategic Framework (2017), Home by the Bay (2023 to 2028) and its year-two progress report, and Public Health's Overdose Prevention Plan (2022) with its 2024 update.
limits: Every reported figure is the department's own account of its own plan. A goal with no reported figure here may be reported somewhere not saved on disk, and the 2017 plan was overtaken by the pandemic and replaced in 2023. Several goals are system-wide outcomes, such as the street count, that no single programme controls.
